results.correct_value: Southwest Ridge via Heather Pass, south of Lewis Lake, Lewis Glacier east moraine, ~7,500 ft ridge notch, second notch, ~400 ft downclimb into the west-face cirque, easy gully to a large notch on the SW ridge, ridge to summit
results.evidence: The Mountaineers' Southwest Ridge route description, and two independent trip reports (one Heather Pass-Lewis Glacier ascent, one from Wing Lake) all describe the Lewis Glacier -> ~7,500-7,600 ft notch -> west cirque -> gully to a large notch on the SW/south ridge line, matching the row's waypoints, itinerary, timing, hazards and descent. The approach/climbing_route/approach_variants text (Horsefly Pass traverse, SE ridge at 7,000 ft, 7,920 ft notch east of summit, north-ridge finish) matches a different east-side route documented in a separate trip report; the beta's south-slope traverse to the SW ridge at 7,400 ft is a real alternate (one report) and is kept as an alternate only.

patches.fact: Ascent line (which side of the peak / which notch)
patches.find: Leave the maintained trail here and traverse climber's-left (south) below Horsefly Pass, holding around 6,400 ft across a broad talus and scree basin beneath the face. Pick a rising traverse line across scree benches and a scree ramp that threads between two low cliff bands to gain Corteo's southeast ridge at about 7,000 ft. From the ridge, work climber's-left up ledges and short rock steps toward a notch at roughly 7,900-7,920 ft just east of the summit block, then finish through blocky class 3 terrain (some parties rope up for a few class 4 moves near the top) to the 8,107 ft summit. All-in, the approach from the trailhead to the base of the face is about 4-5 miles with roughly 2,500 ft of gain to reach the 7,000 ft ridge. Underfoot is loose, downsloping talus and scree for most of the off-trail traverse — a helmet is worth carrying, since the east face sheds rock, especially as the day warms. Snow can linger in the Horsefly Pass basin and across the traverse well into July, so an axe (and possibly crampons) is worth having for early-season attempts.
patches.replace: Leave the maintained trail here and head west across talus, keeping south of Lewis Lake (~5,700 ft), to the crest of the Lewis Glacier's east lateral moraine near 6,400 ft. Follow the moraine onto the glacier remnant and climb southeast, bearing left near the top, to a notch in the ridge at about 7,500 ft. Work west along the ridge to a second notch, downclimb roughly 400 ft of dirt or snow into the cirque under the west face, then take an easy gully up to a large notch on the Southwest Ridge and follow the crest (exposed class 3 with a few class 4 moves) to the 8,107 ft summit. Loose talus and scree cover much of the off-trail travel, and the downclimb sheds rock onto anyone below, so a helmet is worth carrying. Snow lingers on the glacier and on the traverse out of Heather Pass well into July, so bring an axe and crampons for early-season attempts.

patches.fact: Ascent line (which side of the peak / which notch)
patches.expect: This is Corteo Peak's easiest and most commonly climbed line. After significant off-trail travel from the Maple Pass Loop trail, the route crosses the southeast ridge near 6,900 ft, traverses the south slopes, and gains the southwest ridge around 7,400 ft; from there it follows the ridge crest — sustained class 3 scrambling with real exposure in places and some loose rock — to the 8,107 ft summit. A more technical alternate approach (Lewis Glacier to a notch in the northwest ridge, then the west basin) reaches the same southwest ridge with class 2-4 terrain and a short roped/protected section, but the Maple/Heather Pass line described here is the standard way up.
patches.value: This is Corteo Peak's standard line. From Heather Pass on the Maple Pass Loop trail, it passes south of Lewis Lake, follows the Lewis Glacier's east moraine onto the glacier remnant, and climbs to a notch in the ridge at about 7,500 ft; it then works west to a second notch, downclimbs about 400 ft into the west-face cirque, and takes an easy gully to a large notch on the southwest ridge. From there it follows the ridge crest — sustained class 3 scrambling with real exposure in places, a few class 4 moves and some loose rock — to the 8,107 ft summit. An alternate from Maple Pass traverses below Horsefly Pass, crosses the southeast ridge near 6,900 ft and works across the south slopes to join the southwest ridge around 7,400 ft.

patches.fact: Ascent line (which side of the peak / which notch)
patches.expect:
THE TRAVERSE IS HELD AT A HEIGHT AND THE ENTRY TO THE RIDGE IS A RAMP BETWEEN TWO CLIFF BANDS, WHICH IS THE ONE DETAIL THAT MAKES THIS FINDABLE. From Heather Pass, traverse climber's-LEFT, south, BELOW HORSEFLY PASS, HOLDING AROUND 6,400 FT across a broad talus and scree basin beneath the face. Then pick a rising traverse across scree benches and A SCREE RAMP THAT THREADS BETWEEN TWO LOW CLIFF BANDS to gain Corteo's southeast ridge AT ABOUT 7,000 FT.

SO THERE ARE TWO NUMBERS AND ONE SHAPE: HOLD 6,400 FT ACROSS THE BASIN, FIND A RAMP BETWEEN TWO CLIFF BANDS, AND GAIN THE RIDGE AT 7,000 FT. In cloud the altimeter does most of the work and the ramp is the only thing you have to see.

IF YOU CANNOT FIND A WAY THROUGH THE CLIFF BANDS, YOU ARE NOT AT THE RAMP. There is one threading line; forcing a cliff band elsewhere is how this approach goes wrong.

FROM THE RIDGE, work climber's-LEFT up ledges and short rock steps toward A NOTCH AT ROUGHLY 7,900-7,920 FT JUST EAST OF THE SUMMIT BLOCK, then finish through blocky class 3 terrain, with some parties roping up for a few class 4 moves near the top, to the 8,107 ft summit.

SO THE SEQUENCE OF HEIGHTS IS 6,400, 7,000, 7,900, 8,107, AND EACH ONE IS A CHANGE OF GROUND: basin traverse, ridge gained, notch, summit block.

A HAZARD THAT IS ALSO A TIMING INSTRUCTION: underfoot is loose, downsloping talus and scree for most of the off-trail traverse, AND THE EAST FACE SHEDS ROCK ESPECIALLY AS THE DAY WARMS. Cross the basin early.

THE DESCENT USES DIFFERENT GROUND FROM THE ASCENT AND THAT IS WORTH PLANNING FOR: it drops southwest along the ridge crest to a large notch roughly a third of the way down at about 7,600-7,700 ft, reached through an easy connecting gully with ONE DISTINCTLY STEEPER STEP, commonly protected with a single-strand rappel on one 30 m rope off natural gear since no fixed anchor has been reported. Below the step, the gully and talus lead into the west-face cirque near the Lewis Glacier's east moraine at about 6,400 ft, then talus and intermittent boot path south past Lewis Lake rejoin the trail near Heather Pass.
patches.value:
THE ROUTE IS A CHAIN OF NOTCHES, AND THE FIRST ONE DECIDES THE DAY. From Heather Pass, head west across talus, passing south of Lewis Lake (about 5,700 ft), to the crest of the Lewis Glacier's east lateral moraine near 6,400 ft. Follow the moraine onto the glacier remnant and climb southeast, BEARING LEFT NEAR THE TOP, to a notch in the ridge at about 7,500 ft. Bearing right instead puts a party on narrow, sand-covered ledges and a steep, constricted snow gully — a much harder line.

FROM THE FIRST NOTCH, follow the ridge west to a second notch, then DOWNCLIMB ROUGHLY 400 FT of dirt or snow into the cirque under the west face. The ground is loose; space the party out.

FROM THE CIRQUE, an easy gully leads to a large notch on the Southwest Ridge, and the ridge crest — exposed class 3 with a few class 4 moves — goes to the 8,107 ft summit.

SO THE SEQUENCE OF HEIGHTS IS 6,400, 7,500, THE CIRQUE BELOW IT, THE RIDGE NOTCH, 8,107: moraine, first notch, downclimb, ridge gained, summit.

THE DESCENT REVERSES THE SAME LINE, INCLUDING THE CLIMB BACK OUT OF THE CIRQUE TO THE 7,500 FT NOTCH. Fix the notches in your mind on the way up; they are easy to lose from above.
